mechanism: A previously flown aircraft completes REFUELLING for lower-priority BASIC preparation, then is confiscated by later higher-priority SECOND; a direct reference to the built-in REFUELLING subtask should be omitted during SECOND's new preparation while an ordinary equal-duration INSPECT control repeats.

configuration.prep_steps: ten-minute SEQ1 followed by twenty-minute SERVICE SEQ2

hypotheses_to_test: The first BASIC mission flies and returns before the hour-7 preparation, creating post-flight refuelling need in the child.
At the hour-7 BASIC call, the REFUELLING child executes positive-duration SEQ1, then enters SERVICE while the aircraft is confiscated at the 7.25 SECOND call.
SECOND preparation omits positive REFUELLING work after confiscation but still executes SERVICE; the INSPECT control repeats its ten-minute SEQ1 when SECOND preparation begins.

Raw subtask starts, completions, skips or zero-duration markers, mission transfers, flight and cancellation events, report bins and terminal state are reconciled without inferring unreported fuel quantity.
All source business tables roundtrip exactly, conversion errors are zero, native outputs are nonempty, GUI PID and queue guards hold, and the raw files are sealed.
limits: Only one deterministic aircraft with one earlier flight and one active-preparation confiscation; fuel quantity, tanks and consumption are not modeled.
A failed observation is retained as a capability probe, not published as verified refuelling omission.
Payloading, unloading, later flight reset, remote PM reset, resource waiting, GUI-only behavior and cross-engine parity remain unverified.
